subtext.en: Integrated Grammar — 3 types of questions, one strategy
subtext.hi: Integrated Grammar — 3 types ke questions, ek strategy

text.en: Gap filling, editing, and transformation aren't 3 skills — they're 1 habit applied 3 ways. Learn the habit.
text.hi: Gap filling, editing, aur transformation 3 skills nahi hain — ye 1 habit hai jo 3 tarike se apply hoti hai. Wo habit seekho.

content.en:
Type 1: Gap Filling (Cloze Test)

Gap filling mein ek passage hota hai jisme kuch words missing hain. Options diye hote hain ya blanks fill karne hote hain.

Strategy:
1. Passage ko pehle quickly padho — main idea samajh lo
2. Blank ke aas-paas ke words padho — context samajhne ke liye
3. Grammar rule apply karo:
   - Agar noun ke pehle blank hai → Article/Determiner/Adjective
   - Agar subject ke baad blank hai → Verb (tense check karo)
   - Agar do clauses ke beech blank hai → Conjunction (and, but, because, although)
   - Agar verb ke pehle blank hai → Adverb

Example:
She is ___ (a/an) honest girl.
→ 'Honest' vowel sound se start hota hai → an

content.en:
🔍 One Habit That Solves All 3 Question Types

Gap Filling, Editing, and Transformation LOOK like 3 different skills — but they're really testing the SAME thing: can you spot which of the 5 grammar topics (Determiners, Tenses, Modals, SVA, Reported Speech) is being tested in THIS particular blank/line/sentence?

The habit: Before answering, silently label the question — "Is this a tense issue? An article issue? An SVA issue?" Once you've labelled it, you're just applying a rule you already know from the other 5 lessons — you're not learning anything new here, just combining what you already have.

That's why this lesson comes LAST — it's the exam-simulation lesson where all previous lessons get used together, exactly like the real board paper.
content.hi:
🔍 Ek Habit Jo Teeno Question Types Solve Kar Deti Hai

Gap Filling, Editing, aur Transformation 3 alag skills lagti hain — but asal mein SAME cheez test kar rahi hain: kya tum pehchan sakte ho ki 5 grammar topics (Determiners, Tenses, Modals, SVA, Reported Speech) mein se kaunsa is particular blank/line/sentence mein test ho raha hai?

Habit: Answer dene se pehle, chupke se question ko label karo — "Ye tense ka issue hai? Article ka? SVA ka?" Ek baar label ho gaya, tum bas woh rule apply kar rahe ho jo tumhe pehle se pata hai baaki 5 lessons se — yahan kuch naya nahi seekh rahe, jo pata hai usko combine kar rahe ho.

Isliye ye lesson LAST mein aata hai — ye exam-simulation lesson hai jahan saare pehle wale lessons ek saath use hote hain, bilkul real board paper ki tarah.

content.en:
Type 2: Editing (Error Spotting)

Editing mein ek passage diya jata hai jisme errors hain. Har line mein ek error hota hai. Error ko underline karna hai aur correct word likhna hai.

Most Common Error Patterns in CBSE:

1. Tense Errors (40% questions)
   - Simple Present ki jagah Simple Past
   - Present Continuous ki jagah Present Perfect
   - 'Have' + V2 ki jagah 'have' + V3

2. Subject-Verb Agreement (25% questions)
   - Singular subject + plural verb
   - 'Each', 'every', 'neither' ke baad plural verb

3. Article Errors (15% questions)
   - 'A' ki jagah 'an' (vowel sound)
   - 'The' missing before superlative/unique nouns

4. Preposition Errors (10% questions)
   - 'In' ki jagah 'on' (days ke liye)
   - 'At' ki jagah 'in' (cities/countries ke liye)

5. Spelling Errors (10% questions)
   - Double letters missing (beginning, success)
   - Silent letters (honest, hour)

content.en:
Type 3: Sentence Transformation

Sentence transformation mein ek sentence diya jata hai aur usse doosre form mein badalna hota hai bina meaning change kiye.

Common Transformation Types:

1. Assertive → Negative (without changing meaning)
   - She is very intelligent. → She is not dull at all.

2. Assertive → Interrogative
   - He is a good boy. → Is he not a good boy?

3. Simple → Compound
   - Though he is poor, he is honest. → He is poor but honest.

4. Simple → Complex
   - Being tired, he sat down. → As he was tired, he sat down.

5. Active → Passive
   - Ram wrote a letter. → A letter was written by Ram.

6. Direct → Indirect (Already covered in Reported Speech)

Type 3: Sentence Transformation

Sentence transformation mein ek sentence diya jata hai aur usse doosre form mein badalna hota hai bina meaning change kiye.

Common Transformation Types:

1. Assertive → Negative (meaning bina change kiye)
   - She is very intelligent. → She is not dull at all.

2. Assertive → Interrogative
   - He is a good boy. → Is he not a good boy?

3. Simple → Compound
   - Though he is poor, he is honest. → He is poor but honest.

4. Simple → Complex
   - Being tired, he sat down. → As he was tired, he sat down.

5. Active → Passive
   - Ram wrote a letter. → A letter was written by Ram.

6. Direct → Indirect (Pehle hi Reported Speech mein cover kiya)

content.en:
Active → Passive Voice (Important!)

Formula: Object + Helping Verb + V3 + by + Subject

| Tense | Active | Passive |
|---|---|---|
| Simple Present | Ram writes a letter. | A letter is written by Ram. |
| Present Continuous | Ram is writing a letter. | A letter is being written by Ram. |
| Present Perfect | Ram has written a letter. | A letter has been written by Ram. |
| Simple Past | Ram wrote a letter. | A letter was written by Ram. |
| Past Continuous | Ram was writing a letter. | A letter was being written by Ram. |
| Past Perfect | Ram had written a letter. | A letter had been written by Ram. |
| Simple Future | Ram will write a letter. | A letter will be written by Ram. |
| Future Perfect | Ram will have written a letter. | A letter will have been written by Ram. |

Important Rules:
1. Object becomes Subject
2. Verb always becomes V3
3. Helping verb tense ke hisaab se change hota hai
4. 'By + subject' last mein lagta hai
5. Intransitive verbs (no object) ka passive nahi banta: He sleeps. (no passive)

content.en:
🥊 Confusion Buster — Simple→Compound vs Simple→Complex

Both transformations join two ideas into one sentence — but students often can't tell which one is being asked for.

Compound sentence = two EQUAL, independent ideas joined by and/but/or/so (both ideas could stand alone as full sentences)
• "He is poor but he is honest." (both halves are complete sentences on their own)

Complex sentence = one MAIN idea + one DEPENDENT idea joined by because/although/when/if/who/which (the dependent part can't stand alone)
• "Although he is poor, he is honest." ("Although he is poor" can't stand alone as a complete thought)

Quick test: Cover up everything after the joining word. If what's left still makes complete sense alone → compound. If it sounds incomplete/hanging → complex.
content.hi:
🥊 Confusion Buster — Simple→Compound vs Simple→Complex

Dono transformations do ideas ko ek sentence mein jodte hain — but students often bata nahi paate kaunsa poocha ja raha hai.

Compound sentence = do EQUAL, independent ideas and/but/or/so se jude hue (dono ideas apne aap complete sentences ki tarah khade ho sakte hain)
• "He is poor but he is honest." (dono halves apne aap complete sentences hain)

Complex sentence = ek MAIN idea + ek DEPENDENT idea because/although/when/if/who/which se juda (dependent part apne aap khada nahi ho sakta)
• "Although he is poor, he is honest." ("Although he is poor" apne aap complete thought nahi hai)

Quick test: Joining word ke baad sab kuch cover karo. Agar jo bacha hai wo apne aap complete sense banata hai → compound. Agar incomplete/hanging lagta hai → complex.
